subject: Estimated token flow and peak throughput — follow-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Miller <ava@orchid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Estimated token flow and peak throughput — follow-up

Hi Ava — great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks to lock the pricing side down before I hand off to Sales Ops:

Recap from call:
- Expected monthly token volume (your estimate): 180M–250M tokens per month (primary app traffic).
- Typical request shape: ~50 prompt tokens / ~250 response tokens => ~300 total tokens per request.
- Peak sustained TPS (99th pct): ~35–45 TPS. Peak bursts occasionally up to ~60 TPS for ~2–5 minutes.
- Target unit economics you mentioned in-thread: ~$250–$300 per 1M tokens (goal is to keep $/1M <= $300 once committed).

Clarifying asks (so we can produce 2 pricing options):
1) Please confirm a single monthly expected run-rate number within the range (e.g., 200M tokens +/- 10%) that your finance/procurement will sign to for a committed option.
2) Confirm whether bursts to ~60 TPS must be SLA-backed or if graceful throttling/soft-fallback (queueing + 2nd-tier model) is acceptable.
3) Any constraints on model variants (must be on our Llama-3 quantized profile, or open to faster/cheaper quantized-only endpoints?).

What I’ll send next: a one-page MAP (attached) showing two routes — committed monthly slab with discount bands and an on-demand + burst buffer option — plus an illustrative cost table for the 180–250M range. I’ve included a small sample of the request/response token mix we saw in your demo (model-usage-sample.csv).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the single run-rate and burst/SLA preference by EOD Mon (Jul 3).
- I’ll share a draft quote + order form (Sales Ops) by Wed (Jul 5).
- Follow-up call to review contract/redlines on Thu (Jul 6) — Marissa will join from Sales Ops.

Attachments: MAP_Orchid-Initial-v1.pdf, model-usage-sample.csv

Thanks — Ben

From: Ava Miller <ava@orchid.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Estimated token flow and peak throughput — follow-up

Ben — thanks for the write-up and for capturing the numbers cleanly. A few points from procurement/engineering that tweak the framing a bit:

- Confirmed run-rate: we expect to land around 200M tokens/month for Q3, with +/-15% seasonality. Finance would be comfortable with a committed band if we can get clarity on the true-up cadence (monthly vs. quarterly).
- Peak TPS: engineering expects typical peaks around 30–40 TPS. The 60 TPS number is an auto-scaling burst from our traffic generator and is rare; we want an option for a 5–10 minute burst window rather than a permanent SLA at that level.
- Model constraints: we prefer the faster quantized variant if 95% of outputs match our quality bar. Cost is a material concern for us; our internal target is $250 per 1M tokens (or better) on a committed plan.

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to have an executed order by end of July if pricing/terms align. Please include an explicit true-up cadence and a short note about data retention/PII handling for our security team.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Miller
Head of Product | Orchid AI
ava@orchid.ai | +1 646-999-0211

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Jul 2028 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Estimated token flow and peak throughput — follow-up

Thanks, Ava — that all makes sense and helps narrow the options. Short answers inline, then proposed pricing bands: 

- True-up cadence: we can do monthly true-ups with a quarterly reconciliation (most customers pick monthly for visibility + quarterly for settlement). We’ll show both in the MAP.
- Bursts: we offer a burst buffer (charged only if used) for short windows; SLA-backed permanent capacity is available at a higher committed tier. For your use case I recommend the committed slab (200M target) + 1-2M token burst buffer pool to start.
- Model variant: we’ll default to the quantized high-throughput profile and include an optional higher-quality variant for A/Bing; that will be a separate price line.

Illustrative pricing — committed slab (200M target)
- Option A (12mo commit): $225 / 1M tokens effective (committed price; priority capacity; 60-day notice for downscale). Estimated monthly cost: $45,000 for 200M tokens.
- Option B (12mo flexible): $250 / 1M tokens effective (committed, softer capacity guarantees, monthly true-up). Estimated monthly cost: $50,000 for 200M tokens.
- Option C (on-demand + burst): $320 / 1M tokens effective; burst buffer billed at peak-minute usage. Good for pilots or if you want no long-term commit.

I’ve attached a short spreadsheet showing price points across the 180–250M range (pricing-options-Redwood.xlsx). If $225 is compelling we’ll need to capture a 12mo commit and provide a limited credit for a short pilot. If $250 is the target, Option B is the straightforward path that balances cost and flexibility.

Next steps:
1) I’ll get Sales Ops to draft the order form for Option B as your baseline (per your $250 target) and include the monthly true-up language.
2) Marissa — can you confirm you can have a draft order form + SOW by Wed Jul 5 for review?
3) Ava — confirm whether you want the 1–2M burst pool included or prefer pay-as-you-go burst.

Thanks — Ben
